newsitem.title: LATVIA: ZILE SEES T-BILL RATES AS LOW - REPORT.
newsitem.headline: ZILE SEES T-BILL RATES AS LOW - REPORT.

text.p: Government Treasury bill rates are very low and may rise, Finance minister Robert Zile was reported as saying by Dienas Bizness newspaper on Monday.
He also repeated that at the end of April two-year T-bills will be issued and that five-year paper may come either at the end of 1996 or 1997.

"I am not sure whether they will stay as low all the time and whether that is always so good, because falling refinancing rates influence tax debt issues and government income from taxes," Zile told the newspaper in an interview.
Zile was reported as saying that current tax rates are not going to be raised this year but collection would be improved.
"At the moment, we can only speak about increasing the tax base but it will not happen this year," Zile said.
"On May 16 we plan conceptually to review the income tax...creating a joint package of both company and individual income tax," Zile told the newspaper.
"Nothing is going to be changed in the company income tax itself," he was reported as saying.
Zile also said that International Monetary Fund (IMF) was worried about levels of public investment.
"They (the IMF) are ready to accept a budget deficit of 0.5 percent of GDP, rather than a stagnating situation, when investment levels do not grow," Zile added.
Zile also said the current situation shows a balanced budget was possible.
However, problems may arise with municipal budgets as individual income tax collection is lagging behind forecasts, which may be compensated from the basic budget.
